transcript: I gave you a little insight. I mean, I wrote this book back in 15 years ago, 16 years ago about the centrality of family as part of public policy. I've been engaged in family policy only because as a Christian, I understand the importance of being mothers and fathers and families. It's common sense, but as you mentioned, it's also the science of how important that family life is for raising a healthy next generation of Americans. I've always been as a legislator interested in these things. And as you see, as you mentioned, the dynamic of the family has changed dramatically. A majority of children in America today are going to be raised without a father in the home at some point in time. Single-parenthood is becoming more than the norm than the exception. And that makes family life harder. I mean, you can argue one way or another. But the reality is the science is common senses. Children are our best when they have a mom and a dad who's nurturing and supporting them and and bonding with them and giving them the best chance. And so what can we do to to help that situation to foster that situation in America? And I looked at a variety of different things. And when the issue of paid family leave came around, I was frankly cold to the idea back in the 90s when I was in the house. I voted against the Family Medical Leave Act, which was an unpaid leave bill. And because I didn't think that mandating businesses to to provide unpaid lead was was the right approach. But the interesting about this is that we've looked at this issue and said, is there a way to do this without harming small businesses in particular without. putting new taxes on everybody else and new programs. And I give credit to folks like Marco Rubio, your Senator and Bill Cassidy from Louisiana, Kristin Cinema from Arizona and others bi-partisanly who have come together with ideas that don't create new mandates, don't create new taxes, don't create new programs, but use existing programs, existing benefits that flow to families and allow families the flexibility to be able to take those benefits at a time when they choose its most important for them to do. For example, one of the bills says that we have a child tax credit that every year families get, I think it's $2,500 per maximum per child as a tax credit. Well, what if a mom and a dad decided that at the birth of a child, we wanted to take an extended period of time off a month or two months or three months off, why don't we make that child credit available? The child credit that you're going to get for that child over the next five years, let's take a portion of the next five years child credit, move it forward to today, lower your benefit in the future, but give you more benefits today so you can take that time off, so you can spend with that child. You know, you said you wrote down the numbers, maybe your numbers are better than my memory, but the science behind the importance of those first few weeks and months of life of a child is it just mind-blowing how that bonding experience for that child, that child being able to attach to a mom and or a dad, to give that stability and security, just dramatic improvements on mental health, on physical health, on education, on success and employment. I mean, you would say, wow, how can those first few weeks and months of life be that much of a determiner? But the reality is it is that much of a term because you're setting your child at that very early age, all the wiring is being put in place in the brain. And having that sense of love and security and stability is just critical for the development of that child. And so I say to my fellow Republicans, I understand you don't like government programs, you don't like this and that, but you love babies and you care about the future of our country and you want families to be stable and healthy, You just can't, obviously prayer is great, but also doing something is great. And the status quo isn't working for these kids far too many are falling through the cracks, far too many moms and dads are forced to go back to work and that bond isn't established. And we have to do something to change that dynamic. The parental leave provisions that both Marco is advocating, Cassie and others to me is the way to go.
